review.rationale: Methodological contract for draft Test Card T024. The evidence decision lives in docs/standard. Introduction years transcribed from Nordhaus 1997 Table 1.1 (rows realigned against the chapter text); world population downloaded unchanged from Our World in Data.

question: Do intervals between lighting introductions shrink with world population with slope -0.27 (Bettencourt et al. 2007) or -1 (Kremer 1993)?

output.quantity: slope b of log10 interval on log10 world population and its 95 percent interval
output.domain: lighting introductions 3000 BC to the 1980s (11 entries, 10 intervals); world population
output.accuracy: Student t 95 percent interval on the slope; decade labels coded as decade + 5.

model.assumptions: Lighting introductions stand for innovation in general; world population stands for the innovating population.
model.approximation: Decade labels at decade + 5; log-linear population interpolation between listed years.
model.initial_boundary: Primary list and exclusions fixed in the script before the run.
model.drive_environment: Historical world population as compiled by HYDE 3.3, Gapminder and UN WPP.
model.parameters: No fitting of beta; beta = 1.27 from Bettencourt et al. 2007; Kremer slope -1.

data_policy.holdout_policy: No holdout. Both tables seen while transcribing and registering (SEEN_SUMMARY); no slope computed before the card; declared in Test Card T024.

system_partition.boundary: Dated lighting introductions and world population; published tables only.

systems.state: Lighting technologies and the world population that introduced them

couplings.map: Historical dating of lighting introductions and population estimates

observables.quantity: introduction year of each lighting technology and world population in that year

observation.source_state: Lighting technologies and the population that introduced them.
observation.observer_state: Nordhaus 1997 Table 1.1 and Our World in Data compilations.
observation.readout: Efficiency and labor price of light.

components.reason: Introduction years and population as fixed in the card.

error_budget.approximation: Decade labels at decade + 5 shift intervals by up to 5 years; world population instead of the inventing country's.
error_budget.measurement: Historical dates and population estimates without error bars; population before 1800 uncertain by tens of percent.
error_budget.systematic: Table 1.1 rows realigned from a scrambled PDF text layer and checked against the chapter text; the choice of which rows count as new technologies is fixed in the script.
error_budget.omissions: Rows before 10,000 BC and undated rows not used.
error_budget.dependence: Single compilation for dates; single compilation for population.
error_budget.acceptance: Outcome categories fixed in Test Card T024.

claim_boundary: Model selection between two borrowed scaling principles on one technology line and world population; not a UET-distinct prediction and not a test of urban scaling within cities.
next_action: Run done and recorded as FAILED for beta = 1.27; a later card may test Kremer slope -1 on another technology line.
